newsitem.title: FRANCE: F.Telecom sale to boost funds for state companies.
newsitem.headline: F.Telecom sale to boost funds for state companies.

text.p: France said on Wednesday it could raise up to twice as much as it originally expected through the partial privatisation of France Telecom, which would boost funds available to pump into other state-owned companies.

France Telecom head Michel Bon said the government planned to raise between 30 and 50 billion francs ($5.3 and $8.8 billion) from the sale in May of an unspecified stake in France Telecom -- compared to 25 billion francs initially foreseen.
The revenues will help meet a growing bill to plug holes in other troubled state-owned companies, including bank Credit Lyonnais and insurer Groupe GAN.

The finance ministry declined all comment on the actual size of the stake to be sold, though an official said the final amount raised would depend on demand and market conditions. It would remain in any case less than 50 percent.
Under rules in the Maastricht treaty on monetary union, France cannot use privatisation revenues to limit its budget deficit this year.
But it nonetheless needs healthy revenues to pay for capital injections for other state firms, which according to 1997 budget forecasts are to be entirely funded from privatisation proceeds.
"They need a lot of cash injections in all the public sector," ABN-Amro economist Philippe Brossard said.

The government has pledged to reduce the central government budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product this year from 4.1 percent last year to guarantee France a place in the single European currency to be launched in 1999.

It is already using the sale of France Telecom as an excuse to transfer 37.5 billion francs in its books to cover pension liabilities to the government budget -- a move which should enable it to meet its three percent deficit target this year.
The windfall from the privatisation will help deal with another big problem -- shaping up public sector firms for sale, usually requiring public money to make them saleable.
According to government figures released last month, capital injections into state firms announced so far for 1997 came to 32.1 billion francs.

These were to be met by existing and expected privatisation receipts including more than 10 billion francs in unspent revenues from last year and a projected 27 billion francs due this year -- mostly from the partial sale of France Telecom.
Among capital injections planned for 1997 are 11 billion francs for GAN and 11 billion for Thomson Multimedia, the consumer electronics division of the Thomson SA group.
However, the government's February total did not allow for any capital injection into Credit Lyonnais, likely to be the biggest drain on state funds over the next few years.
The total cost of bailing out Credit Lyonnais over a number of years has been estimated at 130 billion francs by a member of a French parliamentary finance committee.
The government, which is seeking European Commission approval for a new rescue plan, has declined to give a figure for the cost of this, nor for the likely charge this year. ($ = 5.65 French Francs)
